March 3 — BikeLoop, a bicycle-sharing service for city residents, has announced that it will begin operating in Norwood next month. The move follows strong results in several mid-sized cities, where BikeLoop's membership keeps rising and customer reviews remain highly positive.

Archive and Library Team Up to Save Old Sea Charts
By Marta Quintana

MADRID (5 May)— The Lisbon Maritime Archive (LMA) has been one of Europe's leading centres for the study of sea travel for more than a century. Researchers at the LMA can examine ship logs, harbour records, and letters written by sailors and merchants. Last month, the archive began a project to protect twenty rare sailing charts given to it by a private collector who purchased them in the 1960s.
"The collector felt that the charts belonged in a place where students and the general public could see them," said archive director Ana Ribeiro. "Our long history of maritime research was the main reason the LMA was chosen."
However, because the LMA mainly stores bound books and printed records, it lacked the tools needed to repair fragile hand-drawn charts. "We are now working with the Copenhagen Paper Conservation Centre to return the charts to their original state," Ms. Ribeiro said. "The centre has lent us special drying tables and lighting equipment." In addition, Henrik Lund, the centre's head conservator, travelled to Lisbon to train archive staff in methods for repairing torn and faded paper. "Our two organisations share a deep respect for historical documents, and we are pleased to support this work," Mr. Lund said. The archive expects the charts to be repaired and on public display by 15 December.

Two Institutions Join Forces to Save Rare Recordings
By Liam O'Connor

SYDNEY (10 August)— The Melbourne Music Heritage Society (MMHS) has promoted Australian folk music for nearly forty years. Members of the public can visit the society to attend concerts, take songwriting workshops, and browse its collection of sheet music. In July, the society started work on preserving 300 reel-to-reel tapes of traditional songs given to it by a retired radio host who recorded them in the 1970s.
"The donor wanted these songs to be heard by future generations," explained society president Oliver Grant. "He chose us because of our close connection with local musicians."
However, since the MMHS concentrates on live performances and education, it did not have the machines needed to play and copy such old tapes. "We are now partnering with the Wellington Sound Archive to transfer the recordings to digital files," Mr. Grant said. "The archive has sent us two tape players in excellent condition." Furthermore, Kiri Walker, a senior audio engineer at the archive, flew to Melbourne to show society volunteers how to clean and handle damaged tape. "Both of our organisations care about keeping musical history alive, and we are glad to contribute," Ms. Walker said. The society expects the digital versions to be available to the public by 1 March.

One key responsibility of every sales associate at Halden Water Systems is to increase the number of homeowners who install our water filtration systems. ―[1]―. To make sure that visitors to our showroom events become paying customers, follow the steps below.

Brightway Fitness Equipment: From the Trade Fair to the Final Sale

The main task of each account representative at Brightway Fitness Equipment is to increase the number of gyms and hotels that buy our treadmills and exercise bikes. ―[1]―. To ensure that the contacts you make at these events turn into orders, follow these guidelines.
First, sign up for an upcoming industry event or plan one in your region. ―[2]―. Examples of events include trade fairs, equipment trials at local gyms, and webinars streamed on our company Web site. Remember to collect business cards from everyone you speak with.
No more than three days after the event, get in touch with the people you met. Focus first on contacts who said they will be replacing old equipment soon and those who asked for price quotes. ―[3]―. Send each of them a short e-mail suggesting a time to visit their facility.
At the visit, be ready to close the deal. Know our product specifications well and be prepared to address any concern the buyer raises. ―[4]―.
Finally, share your success with your team when a contact becomes a customer!
